```
This tutorial describes the current CV3D UI workflow from raw image-volume or 3D-scanning data to checked facet positions, head landmarks, optical metrics, corneal projections, mirroring, and analysis-ready export.

> **Scope**  
> This guide focuses on the image-volume workflow using Fiji/ImageJ, Blender, R, and the CV3D R package. STL-source datasets are mentioned briefly, but the main tutorial assumes that the dataset starts from an image stack or volume.

---

# Overview

CV3D is an interactive workflow for extracting compound-eye surface information from 3D image data. The current UI coordinates several tools:

- **Fiji/ImageJ** for image-volume preprocessing and STL extraction.
- **Blender** for manual cornea extraction, facet-position checking, and head landmarking.
- **R** and the **CV3D R package** for local-height calculations, thresholding, candidate detection, optical metrics, coordinate rotation, corneal projections, and visual quality control.

The main workflow is:

```text
Raw image volume
-> ImageJ preprocessing
-> ImageJ STL extraction for head and eyes
-> Blender cornea extraction
-> R local-height calculation
-> optional R local-height normalization
-> R local-height thresholding
-> R facet candidate condensation
-> Blender facet position checking
-> Blender head landmarking
-> R optical metrics (05A)
-> R global coordinate rotation (05B)
-> R corneal projections (05C)
-> optional eye mirroring
-> Results / Export: analysis-ready tables and QC report
```

```{r fig-01-workflow-overview, fig.cap="Overview of the CV3D workflow from raw image data to analysis-ready compound-eye outputs.", out.width="66%", fig.align="center", fig.pos="H"}
knitr::include_graphics("docs/images/workflow_overview.png")
```
---

# Required software

Install the following before using the UI:

1. **Python** with `PySide6`.
2. **Fiji/ImageJ**.
3. **Blender**.
4. **R** with access to `Rscript.exe`.
5. The **CV3D R package**, installed from GitHub via `devtools::install_github("Pete-s-Lab/CV3D")`.

On Windows, typical executable paths look like:

```text
Fiji/ImageJ:
C:\Users\<user>\Fiji.app\ImageJ-win64.exe

Blender:
C:\Program Files\Blender Foundation\Blender <version>\blender.exe

Rscript:
C:\Program Files\R\R-<version>\bin\Rscript.exe
```

For Fiji/ImageJ, the current mesh extraction workflow uses the **3D Viewer** for threshold preview and manual STL export. Make sure the 3D Viewer is available in your Fiji installation.

---

# Folder structure of the CV3D UI

The CV3D UI should look like this:

```text
CV3D_UI/
|--- CV3D_app.py
|--- README.md
|--- cv3d_helpers/
   |--- imagej/
   |  |--- CV3D_ij_preprocess.ijm
   |  |--- CV3D_ij_mesh.ijm
   |--- blender/
   |  |--- CV3D_blender.py
   |--- r/
      |--- CV3D_R_03A_heights.R
      |--- CV3D_R_03A_plot_raw.R
      |--- CV3D_R_03A2_normalize.R
      |--- CV3D_R_03A2_plot_norm.R
      |--- CV3D_R_03B_threshold.R
      |--- CV3D_R_03B_plot_threshold.R
      |--- CV3D_R_03C_candidates.R
      |--- CV3D_R_QC_facet_overlay.R
      |--- CV3D_R_05A_metrics.R
      |--- CV3D_R_05A_QC_plots.R
      |--- CV3D_R_05B_align.R
      |--- CV3D_R_05B_QC_plots.R
      |--- CV3D_R_05C_projection.R
      |--- CV3D_R_05C_QC_plots.R
```

Only `CV3D_app.py` needs to be started directly. The helper scripts are detected automatically when they remain in the `cv3d_helpers/` folder.

# Starting the app

Open a terminal in the `CV3D_UI/` folder and run:

```bash
python CV3D_app.py
```

The app opens with the left navigation panel and the main workflow area.

```{r fig-03-start-screen, fig.cap="Start screen of the CV3D UI.", out.width="66%", fig.align="center", fig.pos="H"}
knitr::include_graphics("docs/images/start_screen.png")
```
---

# Initial settings

Open the **Settings** page before running the first dataset.

Set the following executable paths:

- **ImageJ/Fiji executable**
- **Blender executable**
- **Rscript executable**

Then click:

```text
Use bundled helper scripts
```

This fills the helper-script paths automatically from the `cv3d_helpers/` folder. Bundled helper paths are stored as relative paths, for example `cv3d_helpers/r/CV3D_R_05C_QC_plots.R`. Executable paths such as Fiji, Blender, and Rscript remain normal system paths because they are outside the bundle.

Then click:

```text
Check R setup
```

If the CV3D R package is missing, use:

```text
Install/update from GitHub
```

The default GitHub repository is:

```text
Pete-s-Lab/CV3D
```

```{r fig-04-settings-page, fig.cap="Settings page. Only executable paths usually need to be set manually; helper scripts can be loaded from the bundled folder.", out.width="66%", fig.align="center", fig.pos="H"}
knitr::include_graphics("docs/images/settings_page.png")
```
---

# Creating or opening a project

Go to **Project Manager**.

Click:

```text
Open / create project folder
```

Choose a folder that will contain the project registry and all CV datasets.

The app creates or loads:

```text
CV3D_project_registry.json
```

This registry stores all datasets in the current project.

```

# Creating a new CV dataset

In **Project Manager**, click:

```text
Create new CV dataset from raw folder
```

Select the raw-data folder for one specimen or dataset. The app assigns the next available CV ID, for example:

```text
CV0001
CV0002
CV0003
```

For each dataset, the app creates an analysis folder, for example:

```text
raw_dataset_01_two_eyes_image_volume/
|--- CV0001_CV3D/
```

This `CVxxxx_CV3D` folder becomes the main analysis folder for that dataset.

knitr::include_graphics("docs/images/create_dataset.png")
```

# Dataset metadata and eye inventory

Go to **Dataset Setup**.

Check:

- source type
- source notes
- eye presence
- anatomical side, if known
- notes for each eye

The current image-volume workflow normally uses:

```text
source_type = image_volume
```

Mark only eyes that are present in the dataset. The workflow buttons for absent eyes remain disabled.

Click:

```text
Save dataset metadata / eye inventory
```

# ImageJ preprocessing

Go to **ImageJ / Source**.

Click:

```text
Launch ImageJ/Fiji preprocessing
```

This opens Fiji/ImageJ and runs the preprocessing macro. The macro performs the interactive image-volume preparation. It creates cropped NRRD files for the head and present eyes and stores the facet-size estimate.

Expected important outputs include:

```text
CVxxxx_CV3D/01_CVxxxx_head.nrrd
CVxxxx_CV3D/01_CVxxxx_facet_size_estimate.csv
CVxxxx_CV3D/eye1/01_CVxxxx_eye1.nrrd
CVxxxx_CV3D/eye2/01_CVxxxx_eye2.nrrd
```

If no rectangular ROI is selected, the macro prompts for ROI selection again.

```

knitr::include_graphics("docs/images/facet_size_estimation.png")
```

# ImageJ STL extraction

After preprocessing, still on the **ImageJ / Source** page, click:

```text
Launch ImageJ/Fiji STL extraction
```

Choose one of the available targets:

```text
head + present eyes
head
eye1
eye2
```

The STL extraction macro uses a downscaled 3D Viewer preview to find a suitable threshold quickly. After the threshold is accepted, the final full-resolution 3D Viewer workflow is used for mesh export.

Expected outputs:

```text
CVxxxx_CV3D/01_CVxxxx_head_ImageJ.stl
CVxxxx_CV3D/eye1/01_CVxxxx_eye1_ImageJ.stl
CVxxxx_CV3D/eye2/01_CVxxxx_eye2_ImageJ.stl
```

Status files and logs are written into `json/` and `logs/` folders, not mixed with scientific outputs.

For example:

```text
CVxxxx_CV3D/json/01MESH_CVxxxx_head_ImageJ_status.json
CVxxxx_CV3D/logs/01MESH_CVxxxx_head_ImageJ_status.txt
CVxxxx_CV3D/eye1/json/01MESH_CVxxxx_eye1_ImageJ_status.json
CVxxxx_CV3D/eye1/logs/01MESH_CVxxxx_eye1_ImageJ_status.txt
```

knitr::include_graphics("docs/images/3dviewer_threshold_preview.png")
```

knitr::include_graphics("docs/images/3dviewer_final_export.png")
```

# Checking ImageJ/source outputs

Click:

```text
Check ImageJ/source outputs
```

The app checks whether expected source files exist. This check is intentionally lightweight for large STL files. It checks existence and file size rather than parsing the full STL.

CV3D currently assumes that coordinates in all imported or generated STL files are in **micrometres (µm)**. This includes externally supplied STL files; no automatic unit conversion is inferred from the STL itself.

The report lists whether the following files exist:

- head NRRD
- head STL
- facet-size estimate CSV
- eye NRRDs
- eye STLs
- selected raw STL for Step 02

```{r fig-12-source-output-check, fig.cap="Source/output check report after ImageJ preprocessing and STL extraction.", out.width="66%", fig.align="center", fig.pos="H"}
knitr::include_graphics("docs/images/source_output_check.png")
```

# Step 02: Blender cornea extraction

Go to **Eye Workflow**.

For each present eye, click:

```text
Launch Blender cornea extraction: eyeX
```

Blender opens with the CV3D helper panel. Use the panel to:

1. Import or continue from the source STL.
2. Select the corneal region manually.
3. Separate the selected region as the cornea.
4. Add/update export modifiers if needed.
5. Recalculate normals.
6. Export the selected cornea and save the `.blend` file.

Expected outputs:

```text
CVxxxx_CV3D/eyeX/02_CVxxxx_eyeX_cornea.blend
CVxxxx_CV3D/eyeX/02_CVxxxx_eyeX_cornea.stl
CVxxxx_CV3D/eyeX/json/02_CVxxxx_eyeX_Blender_task.json
CVxxxx_CV3D/eyeX/json/02_CVxxxx_eyeX_Blender_status.json
```

If an existing Blender file is found, the app warns before overwriting. To continue without replacing previous work, choose:

```text
Open existing and continue
```

```{r fig-13-blender-cornea-extraction, fig.cap="Blender helper panel for cornea extraction.", out.width="33%", fig.align="center", fig.pos="H"}
knitr::include_graphics("docs/images/blender_cornea_extraction.png")
```

```

```

# Step 03A: Local-height calculation

After Step 02 is complete, click:

```text
Launch R local height calculation: eyeX
```

This step converts the corneal STL into triangle-centre/normal points and calculates the local height of each triangle centre relative to a reference plane estimated from a **spherical Euclidean neighbourhood**.

The app asks for the neighbourhood **radius**. The current default suggestion is:

```text
local-height neighbourhood radius = facet_size_estimate x 0.5
```

The intended neighbourhood should span enough of the eye surface that the reference plane represents the underlying corneal curvature instead of following the relief of individual facets. The default is therefore set to half the estimated facet size as a practical starting value and can be adjusted for the dataset.

Expected outputs:

```text
CVxxxx_CV3D/eyeX/03_CVxxxx_eyeX_triangles_normals.csv
CVxxxx_CV3D/eyeX/03_CVxxxx_eyeX_local_heights.csv
CVxxxx_CV3D/eyeX/inspection/03_CVxxxx_eyeX_local_height_threshold_plot.png
```

The local-height table contains several related quantities:

- `local_height`: the raw geometric local height in µm;
- `local_height_col`: a greyscale representation of the raw values;
- `local_height_filtered_col`: the same raw values with the colour range clipped at the 10th and 90th percentiles by default; and
- `local_height_contrast`: a peak-enhanced 0--1 contrast scale. CV3D applies the historical `10^local_height` transform, clips the transformed values at the 50th and 90th percentiles by default, and rescales the result to 0--1.

The exponentiated contrast scale is a monotonic transformation intended to make facet peaks easier to inspect and threshold; it is not a separate geometric measurement.

Where surface normals are available, the local-height QC windows use CV3D's standardised face-on view: the mean unit surface normal defines the viewing direction and the greater face-on eye extent is placed vertically. This changes only the view, not the analysed coordinates. Full-eye comparison representations are centred independently for display and placed side by side at 1.1 reference-eye-width intervals.

```{r fig-15-2-local-heights, fig.cap="Step 03A local-height quality control. The workflow retains the raw geometric height and provides clipped-colour and peak-enhanced contrast representations for inspection and threshold selection.", out.width="66%", fig.align="center", fig.pos="H"}
knitr::include_graphics("docs/images/local_heights_results.png")
```
---

# Step 03A2: Optional local-height normalization

After Step 03A, click:

```text
Normalize local heights (optional): eyeX
```

Normalization is useful when the magnitude of raw facet relief varies across the eye. Within each spherical neighbourhood, CV3D clips the selected local-height values to configurable lower and upper quantiles (10th and 90th percentiles by default), rescales them to 0--1, and averages the values contributed by overlapping neighbourhoods. Points for which no valid local normalization can be calculated remain `NA` rather than receiving an artificial fallback value.

The normalized table includes:

- `local_height_norm`: locally normalized height on a 0--1 scale; and
- `local_height_norm_contrast`: peak-enhanced normalized contrast, calculated from `10^local_height_norm` and rescaled back to 0--1.

Expected output:

```text
CVxxxx_CV3D/eyeX/03_CVxxxx_eyeX_local_heights_normalized.csv
```

```{r fig-16-normalized-local-heights, fig.cap="Local-height normalization quality control. Raw/local contrast and locally normalized representations can be compared while threshold-oriented derived variables remain on a 0--1 scale.", out.width="85%", fig.align="center", fig.pos="H"}
knitr::include_graphics("docs/images/normalized_local_heights.png")
```
---

# Step 03B: Local-height thresholding

Click:

```text
Run local-height thresholding: eyeX
```

The app asks whether to threshold the peak-enhanced contrast derived from:

- raw local heights (`local_height_contrast`), or
- normalized local heights (`local_height_norm_contrast`), if available.

If normalized local heights are present, they are selected by default. Both threshold variables are scaled from **0 to 1**, so the preview range defaults to:

```text
minimum = 0
maximum = 1
```

The app first creates a preview showing the contrast distribution. After inspecting the preview, choose the final threshold within the same 0--1 range. Points at or above that value are retained for candidate condensation.

Expected output:

```text
CVxxxx_CV3D/eyeX/03_CVxxxx_eyeX_local_height_thresholded.csv
CVxxxx_CV3D/eyeX/inspection/03B_CVxxxx_eyeX_local_height.png
```

The thresholded CSV stores the selected 3D points and their 0--1 `height_value`, which is subsequently used as the condensation weight in Step 03C.

---

# Step 03C: Facet candidate condensation

Click:

```text
Run facet candidate condensation: eyeX
```

Step 03C reduces the thresholded local-height point cloud from Step 03B to one candidate point per likely ommatidium/facet. The function does this by iteratively moving nearby high local-height points toward local density modes and then merging points that have converged to the same local maximum.

> **Spatial units:** All mesh and point-cloud coordinates are currently assumed to be in micrometres (µm). The corneal-projection sphere diameter is entered in centimetres in the UI and converted internally to micrometres.


## Parameters

### Neighbour radius

The neighbour radius defines the local search radius around each thresholded point. During each condensation iteration, every point looks for neighbouring points within this radius and moves toward their height-weighted local centre.

A good default is:

```text
0.5 x facet diameter estimate
```

For example, if the facet diameter estimate is 17, a good starting value is 8.5.

Smaller values keep nearby facets more separate but may leave too many candidate points. Larger values merge the point cloud more strongly but can fuse neighbouring facets if set too high.

### Merge radius

The merge radius defines the maximum diameter of a final condensed group. CV3D uses complete-linkage clustering after the iterative movement step: **all pairwise distances within a candidate group must be less than or equal to the merge radius**. This prevents chains of individually close points from bridging two distinct facet peaks.

A good default is:

```text
0.3 x facet diameter estimate
```

For example, if the facet diameter estimate is 17, a good starting value is 5.1.

If the output contains too many duplicate candidates per facet, increase the merge radius slightly. If neighbouring facets are fused into one candidate, decrease the merge radius.

### Height-weight exponent

This controls how strongly local-height values influence the movement of points during condensation.

A value of:

```text
2
```

is a good default. For the non-negative 0--1 contrast values produced by Step 03B, weights are calculated directly as `height_value^weight_exponent`; the values are not shifted before weighting. This gives stronger influence to high-contrast facet peaks while preserving the meaning of the 0--1 scale. A shift is applied only if a custom input height column contains negative values.

Lower values make the movement more spatially even. Higher values make the highest local-height points dominate more strongly.

### Maximum iterations

This is the maximum number of condensation iterations. In each iteration, points are moved toward local height-weighted centres. The process may stop earlier if the points no longer move meaningfully.

A good default is:

```text
8
```

Increasing this value can help if points have not fully converged, but it also increases runtime.

### Step size

The step size controls how far each point moves toward its local weighted centre in each iteration.

A good default is:

```text
0.7
```

A value of 1 would move each point directly to the local weighted centre. Lower values damp the movement and can make the condensation more stable, especially when neighbouring peaks are close to each other.

### Minimum group size

After condensation and merging, groups with fewer points than this value are discarded.

A good default is:

```text
3
```

This removes isolated artefacts and very small noise-derived clusters. If the threshold in Step 03B was very strict and only few points remain per facet, this value can be reduced to 1.

### Candidate point selection

This controls which actual point is written as the final representative candidate for each condensed group.

The default is:

```text
nearest mode point
```

This selects the original point closest to the condensed local mode. It usually gives a stable, anatomically plausible candidate position while keeping the output tied to actual data points.

The alternative is:

```text
maximum-height point
```

This selects the point with the highest local-height value within each group. This may be useful when candidates should sit exactly on the strongest local peak, but it can be more sensitive to noise.

### Cores

This controls how many CPU cores are used for the independent point-condensation calculations. It affects runtime but not the intended scientific result.

For large point clouds, using several cores can speed up the calculation substantially. A good starting value is the app’s suggested maximum core count.

### Suggested summary of default values to start with
Recommended default parameters are relative to the facet-size estimate:

```text
neighbour radius approx. 0.5 x facet diameter
merge radius approx. 0.3 x facet diameter
height-weight exponent = 2
maximum iterations = 8
step size = 0.7
minimum group size = 3
candidate point selection = nearest mode point
```

```{r fig-19-facet-candidate-condensation, fig.cap="Parameter dialog for Step 03C facet candidate condensation. In this example, the minimum group size is set to 1 because strict thresholding leaves relatively few points per facet.", out.width="40%", fig.align="center", fig.pos="H"}
knitr::include_graphics("docs/images/facet_candidate_condensation.png")
```

Expected outputs:

```text
CVxxxx_CV3D/eyeX/03_CVxxxx_eyeX_facet_candidates.csv
CVxxxx_CV3D/eyeX/inspection/03C_CVxxxx_eyeX_facet_candidate_condensation_membership.csv
```

The candidate CSV contains automatically detected facet candidates. These are not final until they have been checked in Blender.
```{r fig-20-facet-candidates-overlay, fig.cap="Automatically detected facet candidates overlaid on the local-height surface.", out.width="50%", fig.align="center", fig.pos="H"}
knitr::include_graphics("docs/images/facet_candidates_overlay.png")
```

# Quality-control plotting

The Eye Workflow page provides several plotting buttons.

Available plots include:

```text
View local-height threshold plot: eyeX
Plot raw local heights 3D (PNG + optional rgl): eyeX
Plot normalized local heights 3D (PNG + optional rgl): eyeX
Plot thresholded local-height points 3D: eyeX
Plot facet candidates on local heights: eyeX
Plot facet positions on local heights: eyeX
```

Candidate/position overlay plots automatically choose the 2D projection with the largest spread. This avoids forcing a bad projection when the eye is tilted.

The static PNGs are saved in the background and are not automatically opened. Where available, the app asks whether to also open an interactive `rgl` 3D window.

```{r fig-21-qc-plot-buttons, fig.cap="Quality-control plotting buttons in the Eye Workflow page.", out.width="40%", fig.align="center", fig.pos="H"}
knitr::include_graphics("docs/images/qc_plot_buttons.png")
```
```{r fig-22-pretty-overlay-plot, fig.cap="Facet candidates or positions overlaid on local-height values using an automatically selected 2D projection.", out.width="50%", fig.align="center", fig.pos="H"}
knitr::include_graphics("docs/images/pretty_overlay_plot.png")
```

# Step 04: Blender facet position checking

After Step 03C, click:

```text
Launch Blender facet position checking: eyeX
```

Blender opens the existing eye-specific cornea `.blend` file and imports the facet candidates into the collection:

```text
CV3D_facet_candidates
```

The candidates remain in this collection. During checking, you can:

- delete false candidates
- move candidates
- add candidates at the 3D cursor
- export the checked candidate set

The checked positions are exported as:

```text
CVxxxx_CV3D/eyeX/04_CVxxxx_eyeX_facet_positions.csv
```

The collection name stays `CV3D_facet_candidates`, but after manual checking the exported CSV is considered the final facet-position file.

```{r fig-23-blender-facet-checking, fig.cap="Blender scene for checking automatically detected facet candidates.", out.width="66%", fig.align="center", fig.pos="H"}
knitr::include_graphics("docs/images/blender_facet_checking.png")
```
```{r fig-24-checked-facet-positions, fig.cap="Checked facet positions before export. The cornea mesh is coloured dark blue here to make the facet-position spheres easier to see.", out.width="66%", fig.align="center", fig.pos="H"}
knitr::include_graphics("docs/images/checked_facet_positions.png")
```

# Step 05: Head landmarking

Head landmarks are specimen-level, not eye-level. They are stored in the parent `CVxxxx_CV3D` folder.

Before launching landmarking, the head mesh must exist:

```text
CVxxxx_CV3D/01_CVxxxx_head_ImageJ.stl
```

Click:

```text
Launch Blender head landmarking
```

Blender opens a specimen-level landmarking file:

```text
CVxxxx_CV3D/05_CVxxxx_head_landmarks.blend
```

The head mesh is imported into:

```text
CV3D_head_mesh
```

The head mesh is visible, selectable, and locked in location, rotation, and scale to reduce accidental movement.

The required landmarks are:

```text
anterior
posterior
left
right
```

Use the 3D cursor to place each landmark, then export them.

Expected output:

```text
CVxxxx_CV3D/05_CVxxxx_landmarks.csv
```

```{r fig-25-head-landmarking, fig.cap="Specimen-level head landmarking in Blender.", out.width="66%", fig.align="center", fig.pos="H"}
knitr::include_graphics("docs/images/head_landmarking.png")
```

# R Analysis after landmarking

After Step 05, go to the **R Analysis** tab. This tab contains the downstream steps that turn checked facet positions and head landmarks into optical and spatial output tables.

The eye-wise sections show available steps for each eye. Steps calculated from original eye data use the normal completion symbol. Steps derived from a mirrored source eye are marked with:

\(\rightleftarrows\)

This means that the values were taken from a mirrored source eye and were not recalculated for the target eye.

```{r fig-29-r-analysis-page, fig.cap="R Analysis page with eye-wise 05A, 05B, and 05C analysis steps.", out.width="66%", fig.align="center", fig.pos="H"}
knitr::include_graphics("docs/images/r_analysis_page.png")
```

## Step 05A: Optical metrics

Step 05A uses the checked facet positions from Step 04 to calculate facet-level optical descriptors. Run this step after the final facet-position CSV exists:

```text
CVxxxx_CV3D/eyeX/04_CVxxxx_eyeX_facet_positions.csv
```

Click the 05A button for the relevant eye. Facet neighbours are identified from **local tangent-plane geometry**: nearby facet centres are projected into a locally fitted surface plane and triangulated there, while candidate links are filtered using their three-dimensional spacing. This avoids assuming that the complete eye is spherical or that the eye centroid is a centre of curvature. Choose the local sampling lattice used for Snyder's calculations; **Hexagonal** is the default, with **Square** available as an alternative. The lattice changes Snyder's eye parameter and sampling frequency, while `acuity_cpd` remains $1/(2\Delta\phi)$ with $\Delta\phi$ in degrees. CV3D reports this as a local anatomical acuity estimate using the interommatidial-angle relationship used by Feller et al. (2020), rather than as a behavioural acuity measurement. The app writes the main optical output files into the eye folder:

```text
eyeX/05A_CVxxxx_eyeX_optic_parameters.csv
eyeX/05A_CVxxxx_eyeX_facet_normals.csv
eyeX/05A_CVxxxx_eyeX_facet_sizes.csv
eyeX/05A_CVxxxx_eyeX_interfacet_angles.csv
eyeX/05A_CVxxxx_eyeX_sampling_acuity.csv
eyeX/05A_CVxxxx_eyeX_optical_summary.csv
```

Important columns in later export tables include:

```text
facet_size_um
interfacet_angle_deg
sampling_lattice
eye_parameter
sampling_frequency_rad
acuity_cpd
```

Use the 05A QC plot buttons to inspect optic parameters, facet normals, and selected labelled metrics. Optic-parameter, facet-normal, and labelled-metric QC plots use the standardised face-on view when facet normals are available. The facet-normal plot asks for normal length as a multiple of facet size; the default is 5 times facet size.

```{r fig-30-r-analysis-05a, fig.cap="05A optical metric outputs.", out.width="75%", fig.align="center", fig.pos="H"}
knitr::include_graphics("docs/images/r_analysis_05a_outputs.png")
```

## Step 05B: Global coordinate rotation

Step 05B places each eye into a specimen-level coordinate frame using the head landmarks from Step 05. It also accounts for the ImageJ crop-log offsets so that eye-local coordinates are first transferred back into the head coordinate reference.

Inputs include:

```text
CVxxxx_CV3D/05_CVxxxx_landmarks.csv
eyeX/05A_CVxxxx_eyeX_optic_parameters.csv
```

Expected outputs include:

```text
eyeX/05B_CVxxxx_eyeX_landmark_referenced_coordinates.csv
eyeX/05B_CVxxxx_eyeX_global_aligned_pointcloud.csv
eyeX/05B_CVxxxx_eyeX_global_coordinates.csv
eyeX/05B_CVxxxx_eyeX_global_rotation_matrix.csv
eyeX/05B_CVxxxx_eyeX_global_coordinate_metadata.json
eyeX/05B_CVxxxx_eyeX_global_coordinate_metadata_roi_reference.csv
```

The 05B QC plot shows the globally aligned eye points together with the specimen landmarks. It is one of the most important checks before creating corneal projections.

```{r fig-31-r-analysis-05b, fig.cap="05B global-coordinate rotation outputs.", out.width="66%", fig.align="center", fig.pos="H"}
knitr::include_graphics("docs/images/r_analysis_05b_outputs_3D.png")
```

## Step 05C: Corneal projections

Step 05C projects the globally aligned facet points onto a projection sphere and writes elevation/azimuth coordinates. These outputs make the compound eye spatially interpretable in a standardized two-dimensional angular coordinate system.

Click the 05C button for the relevant eye. The default projection centre is:

```text
Center between eyes
```

When both real-eye global-coordinate tables are available, **Center between eyes** is the midpoint between the two eye centroids. If only one eye is available, CV3D estimates the between-eye centre by projecting that eye centroid onto the anatomical midline (`x = 0`); the output records whether the centre was measured from both eyes or estimated from one eye. The projection sphere size is entered in centimetres in the dialog and converted internally to micrometres.

Expected output:

```text
eyeX/05C_CVxxxx_eyeX_corneal_projections.csv
```

The 05C QC plot button creates corneal-projection plots, including elevation/azimuth plots and 2D projection views. The optional rgl inspection window can be used for interactive 3D checking.

```{r fig-32-r-analysis-05c, fig.cap="05C corneal projection on a 15 cm sphere.", out.width="66%", fig.align="center", fig.pos="H"}
knitr::include_graphics("docs/images/r_analysis_05c_output_s.png")
```

## Combined two-eye QC plots

At the bottom of the R Analysis tab, below the eye-wise sections, there are two combined QC buttons:

```text
Plot 05B global-alignment QC: both eyes
Plot 05C corneal-projection QC: both eyes
```

These buttons plot `eye1` and `eye2` together when both are available. If only one eye is available, they plot the available eye. Use these plots after mirroring or after processing both real eyes to check that the two eyes occupy the expected positions in the shared coordinate system.

```{r fig-33-r-analysis-05c, fig.cap="05C corneal projections of both eyes on a 15 cm sphere.", out.width="66%", fig.align="center", fig.pos="H"}
knitr::include_graphics("docs/images/r_analysis_05c_both_outputs_s.png")
```

```{r fig-33-2-r-analysis-05c, fig.cap="05C corneal projections of both eyes mapped to 2D.", out.width="66%", fig.align="center", fig.pos="H"}
knitr::include_graphics("docs/images/r_analysis_05c_both_outputs_2D.png")
```

# Mirroring

The **Mirroring** page creates a mirrored target eye from an already processed source eye. This is useful when one eye is missing, damaged, or intentionally replaced by a mirrored copy for a two-eye visualization.

Choose:

- source eye
- target anatomical eye
- mirror plane

The default mirror plane is:

```text
YZ plane
```

Mirroring writes into the actual target eye folder:

```text
eye1/
eye2/
```

Mirroring writes directly into the target eye folder. Re-running mirroring overwrites existing target-eye 04/05A/05B/05C outputs and corresponding QC plots.

Mirroring includes the available outputs from checked facet positions through corneal projections:

```text
04 facet positions
05A optical outputs
05B global-coordinate outputs
05C corneal projections
```

Optical values and corneal projections are mirrored from existing outputs; they are not recalculated. Specimen-level head landmarks are not mirrored. They remain the real landmarks of the head.

After mirroring, Workflow and R Analysis mark mirrored steps with \(\rightleftarrows\). Calculation buttons are disabled for mirrored eyes to prevent mirrored outputs from being replaced by newly calculated values.

---

# Results / Export

Go to **Results / Export**.

This tab creates the analysis-ready handoff outputs for the specimen. It is not meant to perform biological interpretation. Instead, it summarizes the processed eyes, writes clean tables, and creates a compact QC report.

Available actions are:

```text
Generate analysis-ready tables
Generate QC PDF report
Create export ZIP
Open final export folder
```

All outputs created from this tab are written into one final export folder:

```text
CVxxxx_CV3D/06_CVxxxx_results_export/
```

The table export creates:

```text
06_CVxxxx_facet_level_analysis_ready.csv
06_CVxxxx_eye_summary.csv
06_CVxxxx_specimen_summary.csv
06_CVxxxx_export_metadata.json
06_CVxxxx_export_manifest.csv
```

The facet-level table is the main handoff file. It uses code-accessible column names, for example:

```text
cv_id
eye
facet_id
data_origin
mirrored
mirrored_from_eye
mirror_plane
x_global
y_global
z_global
norm.x_global
norm.y_global
norm.z_global
facet_size_um
interfacet_angle_deg
eye_parameter
sampling_frequency_rad
sampling_lattice
acuity_cpd
corn.proj.x
corn.proj.y
corn.proj.z
elevation
azimuth
projection_sphere_center_x
projection_sphere_center_y
projection_sphere_center_z
projection_sphere_radius_um
projection_sphere_size_cm
projection_center_mode
projection_center_source
```

The QC PDF report creates a compact specimen-level document with metadata, summary tables, optic-parameter barplots, and a corneal projection elevation/azimuth plot.

```{r fig-35-results-export, fig.cap="Results / Export page with readiness, table export, PDF report, ZIP export, and final export folder.", out.width="66%", fig.align="center", fig.pos="H"}
knitr::include_graphics("docs/images/results_export_page.png")
```

```{r fig-36-final-export-folder, fig.cap="Final 06 results export folder with analysis-ready tables, report, plots, manifest, and ZIP package.", out.width="66%", fig.align="center", fig.pos="H"}
knitr::include_graphics("docs/images/final_export_folder.png")
```

# Troubleshooting

## Fiji/ImageJ does not start

Check the **ImageJ/Fiji executable** path in Settings. It should point to the executable file, not only the Fiji folder.

## The ImageJ macro cannot find expected NRRD files

Run **ImageJ preprocessing** first and then click **Check ImageJ/source outputs**. The STL extraction step requires the cropped NRRD files from preprocessing.

## 3D Viewer shows more than one surface or old surfaces

Close any open 3D Viewer windows before continuing. If old surfaces remain visible, close the 3D Viewer manually and rerun STL extraction.

## The STL is saved but the app says it is missing

Check whether the STL was saved exactly to the expected path shown by the macro. For example:

```text
CVxxxx_CV3D/eye1/01_CVxxxx_eye1_ImageJ.stl
```

If it was saved into the parent folder or with a different name, move or rename it to the expected path and run **Check ImageJ/source outputs**.

## Blender opens but the CV3D panel is not visible

Open the right sidebar in the 3D View. The panel category is:

```text
CV3D
```

## Step 03A is disabled

Step 03A requires a completed Step 02 cornea STL. Check that the following exists:

```text
CVxxxx_CV3D/eyeX/02_CVxxxx_eyeX_cornea.stl
```

## Normalization is disabled

Normalization requires Step 03A output:

```text
CVxxxx_CV3D/eyeX/03_CVxxxx_eyeX_local_heights.csv
```

## Facet position plotting is disabled

Facet position plotting requires completed Step 04 output:

```text
CVxxxx_CV3D/eyeX/04_CVxxxx_eyeX_facet_positions.csv
```

## R step fails immediately

Check:

- Rscript executable path
- CV3D R package installation
- helper-script paths
- stdout/stderr logs in the eye-specific `logs/` folder

---

## 05A, 05B, or 05C buttons are disabled

Check that upstream outputs exist. In particular:

```text
05A requires eyeX/04_CVxxxx_eyeX_facet_positions.csv
05B requires 05_CVxxxx_landmarks.csv and 05A outputs
05C requires 05B global-coordinate outputs
```

If the dataset was moved, reopen it from Project Manager and run the output checks so the workflow state is rebuilt from files on disk.

## 05B global alignment looks wrong

First check the 05B QC plot. The landmarks should be the real specimen-level landmarks. For mirrored eyes, landmark coordinates should remain unchanged; only eye/facet-derived rows are mirrored.

If the eye appears translated incorrectly, inspect the ImageJ crop-log and the 05B ROI-reference output:

```text
eyeX/05B_CVxxxx_eyeX_global_coordinate_metadata_roi_reference.csv
```

## 05C corneal projection looks shifted

Check the 05C parameters in the task/status JSON and rerun Step 05C if needed. The default projection centre is `Center between eyes`; its provenance is recorded as measured from both eyes or estimated from one eye.

## Mirroring overwrote the target eye

Mirroring writes into the target eye folder and overwrites target-eye 04/05A/05B/05C outputs. Use mirroring only when the target eye should be replaced by a mirrored source eye.

## Results / Export files are missing

All outputs from the Results / Export tab are written to:

```text
CVxxxx_CV3D/06_CVxxxx_results_export/
```

Use **Open final export folder** in the Results / Export tab.

## QC PDF report does not open or is empty

First generate the analysis-ready tables, then generate the QC PDF report. If the source tables contain no valid acuity_cpd or elevation/azimuth values, the report can still be generated, but the corneal projection plot may be empty or labelled as unavailable.

# Appendix: Meaning of the main output files

## ImageJ outputs

- `01_CVxxxx_head.nrrd` - Cropped head volume.
- `01_CVxxxx_head_ImageJ.stl` - Head mesh exported from ImageJ/3D Viewer.
- `01_CVxxxx_facet_size_estimate.csv` - Dataset-level facet-size estimate.
- `eyeX/01_CVxxxx_eyeX.nrrd` - Cropped eye volume.
- `eyeX/01_CVxxxx_eyeX_ImageJ.stl` - Eye mesh exported from ImageJ/3D Viewer.

## Blender Step 02 outputs

- `eyeX/02_CVxxxx_eyeX_cornea.blend` - Eye-specific Blender working file.
- `eyeX/02_CVxxxx_eyeX_cornea.stl` - Extracted corneal STL.

## R Step 03 outputs

- `eyeX/03_CVxxxx_eyeX_triangles_normals.csv` - Triangle centre points and normals from the cornea STL.
- `eyeX/03_CVxxxx_eyeX_local_heights.csv` - Raw local-height values.
- `eyeX/03_CVxxxx_eyeX_local_heights_normalized.csv` - Optional normalized local-height values.
- `eyeX/03_CVxxxx_eyeX_local_height_thresholded.csv` - Points above the selected local-height threshold.
- `eyeX/03_CVxxxx_eyeX_facet_candidates.csv` - Automatically detected facet candidate points.

## Blender Step 04 and Step 05 outputs

- `eyeX/04_CVxxxx_eyeX_facet_positions.csv` - Manually checked final facet positions.
- `05_CVxxxx_head_landmarks.blend` - Specimen-level Blender landmarking file.
- `05_CVxxxx_landmarks.csv` - Head landmarks: anterior, posterior, left, and right.

## R Step 05A outputs

- `eyeX/05A_CVxxxx_eyeX_optic_parameters.csv` - Main facet-level optical-parameter table.
- `eyeX/05A_CVxxxx_eyeX_facet_normals.csv` - Facet positions and normals used for normal QC plots.
- `eyeX/05A_CVxxxx_eyeX_facet_sizes.csv` - Facet-size measurements.
- `eyeX/05A_CVxxxx_eyeX_interfacet_angles.csv` - Interfacet-angle measurements.
- `eyeX/05A_CVxxxx_eyeX_sampling_acuity.csv` - Snyder eye parameter/sampling frequency and local anatomical acuity outputs.
- `eyeX/05A_CVxxxx_eyeX_optical_summary.csv` - Eye-level optical summary values.

## R Step 05B outputs

- `eyeX/05B_CVxxxx_eyeX_landmark_referenced_coordinates.csv` - Eye/facet coordinates translated into the head reference frame before final alignment.
- `eyeX/05B_CVxxxx_eyeX_global_aligned_pointcloud.csv` - Combined aligned point cloud used for QC, including facets and real specimen landmarks.
- `eyeX/05B_CVxxxx_eyeX_global_coordinates.csv` - Facet-level global coordinates and global normals.
- `eyeX/05B_CVxxxx_eyeX_global_rotation_matrix.csv` - Rotation matrix used for the global coordinate transformation.
- `eyeX/05B_CVxxxx_eyeX_global_coordinate_metadata.json` - Metadata for the global coordinate transformation.
- `eyeX/05B_CVxxxx_eyeX_global_coordinate_metadata_roi_reference.csv` - ImageJ crop-log/ROI reference information used to translate eye-local coordinates into the head frame.

## R Step 05C outputs

- `eyeX/05C_CVxxxx_eyeX_corneal_projections.csv` - Facet-level corneal projection coordinates, elevation, and azimuth.

## Results / Export outputs

- `06_CVxxxx_results_export/06_CVxxxx_facet_level_analysis_ready.csv` - Main analysis-ready facet-level export table.
- `06_CVxxxx_results_export/06_CVxxxx_eye_summary.csv` - Eye-level summary table.
- `06_CVxxxx_results_export/06_CVxxxx_specimen_summary.csv` - Specimen-level summary table.
- `06_CVxxxx_results_export/06_CVxxxx_export_metadata.json` - Export metadata and provenance.
- `06_CVxxxx_results_export/06_CVxxxx_export_manifest.csv` - Manifest of exported files.
- `06_CVxxxx_results_export/06_CVxxxx_analysis_ready_export_QC_report.pdf` - Compact QC PDF report.
- `06_CVxxxx_results_export/06_CVxxxx_results_export.zip` - ZIP package of the final export.

---

# End of tutorial

This tutorial covers the workflow through analysis-ready export files and report generation. Later optional biological analyses, such as field-of-view summaries or regional visual specialization, are treated as subsequent downstream analyses rather than core pipeline output.
